newsitem.title: USA: CNB Bancshares to acquire bank in merger.
newsitem.headline: CNB Bancshares to acquire bank in merger.

text.p: CNB Bancshares Inc and BMC Bancshares Inc said Friday they signed a definitive agreement to merge.
BMC, based in Mt. Carmel, Ind., has assets of $104 million. It is the holding company for Bank of Mt. Carmel.

Under the agreement, BMC shareholders will receive 884,227 shares of CNB common stock, subject to adjustment if the market price of CNB's stock is below $25.71, or about $28.57 a share during a future pricing period.
In no event, the companies said, will CNB issue more than 1,180,960 shares or fewer than 721,782 shares in the merger.
For example, based on the October 10 closing price of 29-1/2, CNB would issue 856,351 shares in the merger and the value to BMC shareholders would be $25.3 million.
The merger is subject to approval by BMC shareholders, the receipt of regulatory approvals and certain other conditions.
The merger will be accounted for as a pooling of interests and is expected to close in the first quarter of 1997.

"This merger is a natural extension of our seven branches in Gibson County, Indiana, which are just across the Indiana/Illinois border from Mt. Carmel," Jim Giancola, CNB president, said in a statement.
With a new Toyota manufacturing facility being constructed in Princeton, Ind., CNB is expecting "explosive growth" in the area.
CNB, the second largest banking organization in Indiana, has assets of $4 billion.
